ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Context-versus-prior-knowledge likelihood ratio to flag hallucinations in retrieval-augmented answers
PROPOSAL: Score each response token by how far its log-probability rises when the retrieved passage is added to the question, and by how much of that log-probability survives when the passage is removed. Combine the two quantities into a response-level ratio through a logistic layer, so that attention heads and layers need not be chosen. Generate answers with Llama-2-7B-chat, Llama-2-13B-chat and Mistral-7B-Instruct on RAGTruth, covering question answering, summarisation and data-to-text, then compute the scores with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, a model that did not write them. Report area under the ROC curve and F1 per task type on the benchmark's own test partition.
CONTROLS: Compare the ratio against ReDeEP and a token-entropy detector on the same test partition. Compare the ratio against each of its two components used alone on the same partition. Compare a scorer that differs from the generator with a scorer identical to the generator. Compare real passages with passages exchanged between unrelated queries, to check that the external signal tracks the supplied context.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The ratio should reach an area under the curve near 0.80 on question answering and a little lower on summarisation. The claim is refuted when the ratio scores within one point of its better single component, or when scorer mismatch cuts the area by more than 0.1.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Counterfactual passage scoring of answer reliance in retrieval-augmented generation
PROPOSAL: For every sentence of a response, measure the drop in conditional likelihood when the supplied passage is replaced by an empty string, and the drop when the question is replaced by a generic instruction. Pool sentences with a maximum and give the two pooled numbers to a gradient-boosted classifier, which avoids any choice of attention heads or layers. Collect answers from Gemma-2-9B-it, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct on the RAGTruth question-answering and data-to-text subsets, and score them with Mistral-7B-Instruct as an outside model. Give area under the ROC curve, precision at 90 percent recall and F1 for each subset.
CONTROLS: Compare the contrast against a closed-book self-consistency detector and a response-length classifier on the same test partition. Compare the contrast against each of two off-the-shelf sentence-similarity scores used alone on the same partition. Compare a scorer larger than the generator with a scorer smaller than the generator. Compare real passages with passages cut to their first half, to check that the external signal tracks passage length.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Area under the curve should land near 0.78 on question answering and lower on data-to-text. The claim is refuted when the contrast scores within one point of its better pooled number, or when outside-scorer mismatch cuts the area by more than 0.1.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Validating utilization scores by intervening on the retrieved context
PROPOSAL: Build a pair of utilization scores from the shift in next-token distribution, measured by Jensen-Shannon divergence, between the question-plus-passage prompt and the question-only prompt for external use, and between the question-only prompt and a prompt with an unrelated passage for internal use. Validate causally on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with CounterFact-style conflict items placed in a passage: rewrite the passage fact and track external use rising while internal use falls. Then train a small classifier on both scores to detect hallucinations on RAGTruth and the news-summarisation items of FaithBench, reporting area under the curve and F1.
CONTROLS: Compare responses on passages edited to contradict the model's prior knowledge with responses on unedited passages. Compare the classifier on both scores with the classifier on each score alone. Compare items whose answer the model knows without a passage with items whose answer it does not know. Repeat the validation on a second model family to check that the effect carries across models.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: External use should rise and internal use should fall after a passage edit, with the classifier reaching about 0.78 area under the curve. The test fails if either score moves in the wrong direction after an edit, or if the joint classifier gains under two points over its better single score.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Entropy-shift utilization scoring with passage perturbation for hallucination detection
PROPOSAL: Compute external use as the drop in output entropy when the passage is appended, and internal use as the entropy remaining when the passage is replaced by a neutral filler text. Probe the scores on Mistral-7B-Instruct with Wikipedia-derived items in which a date or a name is edited inside the passage, and follow how both scores move after the edit. Fit a decision-tree ensemble on both scores for hallucination detection on RAGTruth and the summarisation part of FaithBench, and report area under the curve and F1.
CONTROLS: Compare responses on passages edited to change their length with responses on unedited passages. Compare the classifier on both scores with the classifier on the sampling temperature alone. Compare items whose passage opens with a date with items whose passage does not. Repeat the validation at a second decoding temperature to check that the effect carries across temperatures.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Both scores should move after a passage edit, with the classifier reaching about 0.76 area under the curve. The test fails when either score moves in the wrong direction after an edit, or if the joint classifier gains under two points over its better single score.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-generator transfer of a context-utilization hallucination detector
PROPOSAL: Train a gradient-boosted detector on utilization features computed by Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct over responses written by Llama-2-7B-chat, then test it on responses written by Llama-2-13B-chat, Mistral-7B-Instruct and GPT-4 on the RAGTruth question-answering and summarisation subsets. Features are the maximum and the 90th percentile of per-token likelihood gain from the passage and of the likelihood retained without it, so that attention heads and layers need not be selected. Report area under the curve, F1 and calibration error for each generator, plus the Spearman link between each feature and the human span annotations.
CONTROLS: Compare held-out generators with the training generator on the same annotated subsets. Compare the detector with a detector trained directly on each target generator's own responses. Compare passages that fully support the answer with passages that omit part of it. Compare the scorer on answers it wrote with answers written by another model.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: Area under the curve should drop by about 0.05 on unseen generators, with the largest drop for GPT-4. The claim fails when the drop passes 0.15 on any generator, or if the transferred detector scores below the in-generator detector by that amount on summarisation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: In-distribution reliability of a utilization-based hallucination detector across question sets
PROPOSAL: Fit a decision-tree ensemble on utilization features computed by Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct over responses that Llama-2-7B-chat wrote, then evaluate it on fresh questions answered by that same Llama-2-7B-chat on the RAGTruth question-answering subset and on closed-book TriviaQA answers, with Mistral-7B-Instruct and GPT-4 used only to paraphrase the questions. Features are the maximum and the 90th percentile of per-token likelihood gain from a passage and of the likelihood retained without it, so that attention heads and layers need not be selected. Report area under the curve, F1 and calibration error for each question set, plus the Spearman link between each feature and the human span annotations.
CONTROLS: Compare held-out questions with the training questions from the same generator on the same annotated subsets. Compare the detector with a detector trained on a larger share of that generator's own responses. Compare answers given with a supporting passage with answers given in closed-book mode. Compare the scorer on answers it wrote with answers written by Llama-2-13B-chat.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: Area under the curve should drop by about 0.03 on held-out questions, with the largest drop for closed-book answers. The claim fails when the drop passes 0.15 on any question set, or if the closed-book detector scores below the in-subset detector by that amount.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Checking that utilization scores track real use of context and prior knowledge
PROPOSAL: Construct for each RAGTruth item three prompt variants: the passage intact, the passage with the decisive sentence removed, and the question alone. Define external use as the loss in answer likelihood when the decisive sentence is removed, and internal use as the likelihood kept with the question alone. Validate on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct by testing against human span labels marking which response spans come from the passage, then supply both scores to a logistic detector assessed on RAGTruth and the news-summarisation items of FaithBench, reporting area under the curve and F1.
CONTROLS: Compare each score with the human span labels at the span level. Compare scores on spans labelled as copied from the passage with spans labelled as drawn from prior knowledge. Compare detector area under the curve with the area of a detector given only the human span labels. Compare the scores before and after the decisive sentence is removed.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: External use should correlate near 0.5 with copied spans and internal use with prior-knowledge spans. The claim is refuted if either correlation stays under 0.2, or if the detector loses more than 0.05 area under the curve when the scores are replaced by span labels.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Relating utilization scores to the size of the answer and the prompt
PROPOSAL: Take each RAGTruth item in three forms: unchanged, trimmed to its first paragraph, and question only. Define external use as the drop in answer likelihood after trimming, and internal use as the likelihood retained with the question only. Examine Mistral-7B-Instruct on a subset of 500 items, relating both scores to the token counts of the response, then provide both scores to a logistic detector assessed on RAGTruth and the news items of FaithBench, giving area under the curve and F1 for each task type.
CONTROLS: Compare each score with the response length at the response level. Compare scores on responses labelled as long with responses labelled as short. Compare detector area under the curve with the area of a detector given only the response length. Compare the scores before and after the answer is lowercased.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: External use should correlate near 0.5 with response length and internal use with question length. The claim is refuted when either correlation stays under 0.2, or if the detector loses more than 0.05 area under the curve when the scores are replaced by length.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Memory-conflict test of a utilization-based hallucination detector
PROPOSAL: Build conflict items in which the retrieved passage contradicts what the model memorised, using entity swaps on Natural Questions and PopQA passages, plus items where the passage agrees with memory. Compute context use and memory use from likelihood shifts under passage removal on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, then train a logistic detector on RAGTruth and evaluate it on the conflict items. Report area under the curve, the fraction of responses that follow memory over the passage, and F1.
CONTROLS: Compare conflict items with agreeing items on the same questions. Compare the detector with a detector that sees response length and passage length only. Compare responses that follow the passage with responses that follow memory, on the conflict items. Compare the two models on the same conflict items.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: Memory use should be larger on conflict items than on agreeing items, with the detector reaching about 0.75 area under the curve. A miss shows as memory use that stays level across the two item types, or as a drop below 0.65 area on conflict items.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Passage-versus-memory scoring on assembled question collections
PROPOSAL: Assemble two collections of items from Natural Questions and PopQA: one in which an entity swap in the passage contradicts memorised facts, and one drawn from unrelated topics with passages that agree with memory. Derive context use and memory use from likelihood shifts under passage removal on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, then fit a logistic detector on RAGTruth and evaluate it on both collections. Report area under the curve, the fraction of responses that follow memory over the passage, and F1.
CONTROLS: Compare conflict items with agreeing items on different questions. Compare the detector with a detector that sees response length and question length only. Compare responses that follow the passage with responses that follow memory, on the agreeing items. Compare the two models on different conflict items.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: Memory use should be larger on the first collection than on the second, with the detector reaching about 0.75 area under the curve. A miss shows as memory use that stays level across the two collections, or as a drop below 0.65 area on the first collection.
